description: Look up which third-party apps Dock can connect (Gmail, Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Granola...), with each app's name and a short description. Use it BEFORE telling anyone that Dock does or does not have an app, and when someone asks 'do you have X?' or 'what can I connect for CRM?'. It only reads: it connects nothing, shows no card and grants nothing. Pass `query` (an app name, a misspelling of one, or a word describing what it does, e.g. "hubspot", "granola mcp", "crm"). The answer has `offered: true` only when an app with that exact name or slug is connectable; otherwise `offered: false` and any close matches are listed under `matches`, so say plainly that Dock does not offer it rather than guessing. Each result also says where it stands for your owner: `connected` (and you can use it), `connected_not_shared` (connected, but not shared with you), or `not_connected`. Without `query` it returns only what your owner already has connected and how many apps Dock offers in total; it never dumps the whole catalogue, so search by name or topic. To put a Connect card in front of your owner, call request_connection with the app's `slug` (in Dock chat), or create_owner_link with `kind: "connect_app"` and the `slug` (over iMessage or text, where cards are not visible). If `already_connected` or `connected_not_shared` comes back, follow what request_connection tells you rather than asking again.

query.description: An app name or slug, a likely misspelling, or a word for what it does. Max 100 characters.

name: list_connectable_apps
